evals.prompt: I sent a message to my worker session with `agent-deck session send worker1 "status?" --json` and it printed delivery:"queued". Did that actually reach Claude or did it fail?
evals.expected_output: Explains `queued` is an exit-0, non-failure outcome specific to Claude targets (message landed while the target was mid-turn and Claude will pick it up when its current turn ends), reads the stable `confirmation` field (here `unknown`, not `failed`) rather than treating `queued` as an error, and does not tell the user to resend.

evals.prompt: Audit the context window bloat across all my agent-deck sessions and tell me which ones are worth cleaning up, without disturbing anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck list --json` then `agent-deck session context <id>` (or `--tab breakdown --all`) per session — read-only, never passes `--verify` (which mutates the live session) without explicit confirmation, and reports findings without editing another session's files.

evals.prompt: Launch 4 child sessions to each fix lint errors in a different package of this monorepo, and let me know when they're all done without me having to keep checking.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck launch <path> -c claude --inherit-group -m "..."` per child (not a custom `-g`), and for the non-blocking notification either backgrounds `agent-deck session children --follow --until-done` or polls `session children --json`, rather than blocking the whole session on one `--wait` send.

evals.prompt: My conductor session's tmux server also runs a webhook listener I built as another agent-deck session. It keeps dying silently and nothing restarts it. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that agent-deck manages interactive sessions, not always-on daemons/listeners, and recommends running the listener under launchd/systemd instead of as a bare agent-deck session (citing the 'What agent-deck is NOT' section), rather than proposing a home-grown agent-deck-based supervisor loop.

evals.prompt: I want a conductor that watches my other sessions and pings me on Telegram when something needs my input, but I also don't want every child session's Claude process to load the Telegram plugin.
evals.expected_output: Recommends activating Telegram per-session via `--channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official` on the conductor only, keeping `enabledPlugins` for that plugin absent/false globally, and warns about the many-competing-pollers gotcha (409 conflicts) if it were enabled globally.

evals.prompt: A worker of mine just told me 'PR #142 is merge-ready, clean diff.' Should I trust that and merge it?
evals.expected_output: Applies the Trust-but-Verify rule: treats the claim as unverified until an independent peer/root session re-derives it from primary sources (`gh pr checkout 142 && go test -race ./...` plus `gh pr view 142 --json mergeable,statusCheckRollup`), and does not accept a same-session self-review as sufficient.

evals.prompt: I registered a remote named 'lab' with an older agent-deck build. Can I update it from my newer controller, and how would I know it actually worked?
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck remote update lab` (or `--all`), mentions the checksum/version verification and that `remote list --check --json` (or the VERSION column) confirms the new version afterward, and does not suggest manually scp'ing a binary onto the remote.

evals.prompt: Set this session's Claude account from personal to a 'client-acme' account slot, keeping the whole conversation history.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck session switch-account <session> client-acme` (or the `session set <session> account` low-level equivalent followed by a restart), and notes the conversation `.jsonl` is copied (not moved) so the old account keeps its copy, and that a name not present in `agent-deck accounts` will error.

agent_friendliness_evals.description: Checks that an agent using this skill treats agent-deck as a well-behaved CLI: reads structured output instead of parsing text, respects documented exit codes, never expects an interactive prompt from a non-TTY context, and stays inside the documented performance budgets. Added per maintainer request (2026-09-18).
checks: Every documented command has --help and --json where output exists
Exit codes are treated as documented and stable (not re-derived from parsing stdout text)
A non-TTY/scripted caller never triggers an interactive screen (e.g. session context --verify without --yes, or --attach without a TTY)

Timings stay inside the health budgets referenced by `agent-deck health`: list --json under 1s at ~100 sessions, session show under 250ms, a send verdict returns without waiting on the completion-ledger journal to fsync

evals.prompt: Write the exact command and how you'd parse its output to check whether a `session send` actually got picked up by the target, for use in an unattended script.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck session send <id> "..." --json` and reads the `confirmation` field (confirmed/unknown/failed) — not string-matching the human-readable line, not re-parsing the fine-grained `delivery` value as if it were the pass/fail signal.

evals.prompt: You're writing a cron job (no TTY) that needs to check what's in a session's context window periodically. Give the exact command.
evals.expected_output: Uses `agent-deck session context <id> --json` (or --tab breakdown --json), and explicitly avoids `--verify` (or if included, pairs it with `--yes`) since `--verify` without `--yes` blocks on a confirmation prompt that a non-TTY cron job can never answer.

evals.prompt: How would you script a check that fires only when `agent-deck list --json` is taking too long on a box with about 100 sessions?
evals.expected_output: References the ~1s budget for `list --json` at that scale (e.g. via `time agent-deck list --json` or `agent-deck health --json` budgets) and treats a stall past that as worth investigating with `agent-deck health`, rather than assuming JSON output itself needs custom timeout-handling beyond a normal process timeout.

evals.prompt: A teammate wants to know: if `session send --json` returns quickly, does that guarantee the completion event already landed in the receiving session's durable inbox?
evals.expected_output: Explains no — send's fast return is about delivery to the pane/socket, not about the inbox/completion-ledger journal, which is a separate durable channel (`inbox drain`) that a worker's own completion sentinel populates later; does not conflate the two.

evals.prompt: Check what exit code `agent-deck session show <id>` uses when the session doesn't exist, and whether that's something you can rely on across versions without re-checking stderr text.
evals.expected_output: Points to the Exit Codes section of cli-reference.md as the source of truth, treats the documented exit code as the stable contract (not incidental stderr wording), and flags that this should be verified against `--help`/cli-reference.md for the installed version rather than assumed from memory.
